sentences.en: While I was working on this story, I watched a worker clean out the apartment of a man who had recently died.
sentences.zh: 在撰写这篇报道时，我看着一名工人清理了一位刚去世男子的公寓。

sentences.en: He opened a closet and found a pair of work boots.
sentences.zh: 他打开壁橱，发现了一双工作靴。

sentences.en: They were totally clean.
sentences.zh: 它们非常干净。

sentences.en: Apparently, they had never been worn.
sentences.zh: 显然，它们从未被穿过。

sentences.en: He tried them on, and they weren't the right size, but they were close enough.
sentences.zh: 他试穿了一下，虽然尺码不太合适，但也差不离。

sentences.en: So he laced them up and continued cleaning out the apartment wearing the dead man's boots.
sentences.zh: 于是他系好鞋带，穿着死者的靴子继续清理公寓。

sentences.en: I'm Sonny Clinefield.
sentences.zh: 我是桑尼·克莱恩菲尔德。

sentences.en: I'm a freelance writer and a former reporter on the Metro staff of the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是一名自由撰稿人，曾是《纽约时报》大都会版的工作记者。

sentences.en: I wrote a story about what happens when you die alone in New York City.
sentences.zh: 我写了一篇关于在纽约市孤独死去会发生什么的报道。

sentences.en: you know the thing about new york it's this jam-packed vibrant city you live sandwiched
sentences.zh: 你知道纽约的特点吗？它是一个拥挤而充满活力的城市，你生活在

sentences.en: beside and beneath and above multitudes of others you fight your way down sidewalks you're just
sentences.zh: 无数人的身旁、脚下和头顶，你在人行道上艰难穿行，你只是

sentences.en: smothered by all this humanity but in back in your homes many people they live the loneliest of
sentences.zh: 被所有这些人群所淹没，但在你的家中，许多人却过着最孤独的

sentences.en: lives i wonder what happens in instances like that when someone dies and there's no one to
sentences.zh: 生活。我很好奇在那种情况下会发生什么，当某人去世而没有人

sentences.en: arrange a funeral and a burial and no one makes any claim on the possessions of that person's life.
sentences.zh: 来安排葬礼和安葬，也没有人对那个人的生前财产提出认领时。

sentences.en: So I found that there was a public administrator who handles cases like that.
sentences.zh: 所以我发现有一位公共行政官专门处理这类案件。

sentences.en: And I approached them and told them I wanted to follow a case from beginning to end and find out just what does happen.
sentences.zh: 我联系了他们，告诉他们我想从头到尾跟踪一个案例，看看究竟会发生什么。

sentences.en: And they came back to me with a case that they thought I might want to look into.
sentences.zh: 他们回馈给我一个他们认为我可能想调查的案件。

sentences.en: At the beginning, all they knew was that it was a 72-year-old man who apparently had died in his apartment in Queens.
sentences.zh: 起初，他们只知道那是一名72岁的男子，显然是在他位于皇后区的公寓里去世的。

sentences.en: The apartment belonged to someone named George Bell.
sentences.zh: 这间公寓属于一个叫乔治·贝尔的人。

sentences.en: It actually took months before they even confirmed that that's who it was.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们花了几个月时间才确认死者确实是他。

sentences.en: So during the process, the public administrator's office looked through George Bell's bank accounts.
sentences.zh: 因此在处理过程中，公共行政官办公室查阅了乔治·贝尔的银行账户。

sentences.en: They took whatever possessions they thought had any value, his car, his watch, and they auctioned them off.
sentences.zh: 他们拿走了他们认为有价值的任何财产，比如他的车、他的手表，并将它们拍卖了。

sentences.en: He learns a lot about what George Bell had, but nothing in the process about who George Bell was.
sentences.zh: 他了解了很多关于乔治·贝尔拥有什么的信息，但在整个过程中，对乔治·贝尔本人却一无所知。

sentences.en: I knew I wanted to tell that story, too.
sentences.zh: 我知道我也想讲述那个故事。

sentences.en: So here's my article from 2015,
sentences.zh: 这是我2015年的文章，

sentences.en: The Lonely Death of George Bell, read by Arthur Horry.
sentences.zh: 《乔治·贝尔的孤独死亡》，由亚瑟·霍里朗读。

sentences.en: They found him in the living room, crumpled up on the mottled carpet.
sentences.zh: 他们在客厅里发现了蜷缩在斑驳地毯上的他。

sentences.en: The police did.
sentences.zh: 是警察发现的。

sentences.en: Sniffing a fetid odor, a neighbor had called 911.
sentences.zh: 闻到一股恶臭后，邻居拨打了911。

sentences.en: The apartment was in north-central Queens, in an unassertive building on 79th Street in Jackson Heights.
sentences.zh: 公寓位于皇后区中北部，在杰克逊高地79街一栋不起眼的建筑里。

sentences.en: The apartment belonged to a George Bell.
sentences.zh: 这间公寓属于乔治·贝尔。

sentences.en: He lived alone.
sentences.zh: 他独居。

sentences.en: Thus, the presumption was that the corpse also belonged to George Bell.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们推测尸体也属于乔治·贝尔。

sentences.en: It was a plausible supposition, but it remained just that, for the puffy body on the floor was decomposed and unrecognizable.
sentences.zh: 这是一个合理的推测，但仅仅只是推测，因为地板上那具浮肿的尸体已经腐烂，无法辨认。

sentences.en: Clearly the man had not died on July 12th, the Saturday last year when he was discovered, nor the day before, nor the day before that.
sentences.zh: 显然，这名男子并不是在去年7月12日那个周六被发现时去世的，也不是前一天或再前一天去世的。

sentences.en: He had lain there for a while, nothing to announce his departure to the world, while the hyperkinetic city around him hurried on with its business.
sentences.zh: 他已经在那里躺了一段时间，没有任何东西向世界宣告他的离去，而他周围那个极度亢奋的城市仍在匆忙地运转。

sentences.en: Neighbors had last seen him six days earlier, a Sunday.
sentences.zh: 邻居们最后一次见到他是在六天前的周日。

sentences.en: On Thursday, there was a break in his routine.
sentences.zh: 周四，他的生活规律出现了中断。

sentences.en: The car he always kept out front and moved from one side of the street to the other to obey parking rules sat on the wrong side.
sentences.zh: 他平时总是停在外面，为了遵守停车规定而从街道一侧移到另一侧的车，停在了错误的一侧。

sentences.en: A ticket was wedged beneath the wiper.
sentences.zh: 雨刷下夹着一张罚单。

sentences.en: The woman next door called Mr. Bell.
sentences.zh: 隔壁的女人给贝尔先生打了电话。

sentences.en: His phone rang and rang.
sentences.zh: 他的电话响个不停。

sentences.en: Then the smell of death and the police and the sobering reason that George Bell did not move his car.
sentences.zh: 随后是死亡的气息、警察的到来，以及乔治·贝尔没有挪车的令人清醒的原因。

sentences.en: Each year, around 50,000 people die in New York, and each year the mortality rate seems to graze a new low, with people living healthier and longer.
sentences.zh: 每年约有5万人死于纽约，每年的死亡率似乎都在触及新低，人们生活得更健康、更长寿。

sentences.en: A great majority of the deceased have relatives and friends who soon learn of their passing and tearfully assemble at their funeral.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数死者都有亲友，他们很快就会得知死讯，并含泪聚集在葬礼上。

sentences.en: A reverent death notice appears.
sentences.zh: 一份庄重的讣告会出现。

sentences.en: Sympathy cards accumulate.
sentences.zh: 慰问卡堆积如山。

sentences.en: When the celebrated die, or there is some heart-rending killing of the innocent, the entire city might weep.
sentences.zh: 当名人去世，或发生令人心碎的无辜者遇害事件时，整个城市可能会为之哀悼。

sentences.en: A much tinier number die alone in unwatched struggles.
sentences.zh: 有极少数人是在无人关注的挣扎中孤独离世的。

sentences.en: No one collects their bodies.
sentences.zh: 没有人收殓他们的遗体。

sentences.en: No one mourns the conclusion of a life.
sentences.zh: 没有人为生命的终结而哀悼。

sentences.en: They're just a name added to the death tables.
sentences.zh: 他们只是死亡名单上增加的一个名字。

sentences.en: In the year 2014, George Bell, age 72, was among those names.
sentences.zh: 2014年，72岁的乔治·贝尔就在这些名字之中。

sentences.en: George Bell.
sentences.zh: 乔治·贝尔。

sentences.en: A simple name.
sentences.zh: 一个简单的名字。

sentences.en: Two syllables.
sentences.zh: 两个音节。

sentences.en: The minimum.
sentences.zh: 最低限度。

sentences.en: The minimum.
sentences.zh: 最低限度。

sentences.en: There were no obvious answers as to who he was or what shape his life had taken, what worries weighed on him, whom he loved, and who loved him.
sentences.zh: 关于他是谁，他的生活是什么样子的，什么烦恼困扰着他，他爱谁，谁爱他，这些都没有明确的答案。

sentences.en: Like most New Yorkers, he lived in the corners, under the pale light of obscurity.
sentences.zh: 像大多数纽约人一样，他生活在角落里，生活在默默无闻的微光下。

sentences.en: Yet death, even in such forlorn form, can cause a surprising amount of activity, setting off an elaborate, lurching process that involves a hodgepodge of interlocking characters
sentences.zh: 然而，即使是以如此凄凉的形式，死亡也能引发惊人的活动，启动一个复杂的、蹒跚的过程，涉及一群形形色色、相互交织的人物，

sentences.en: whose livelihoods flow in part or in whole from death.
sentences.zh: 他们的生计部分或全部源于死亡。

sentences.en: With George Bell, the ripples from the process would spill improbably and seemingly by happenstance from the shadows of Queens to upstate New York and Virginia and Florida.
sentences.zh: 对于乔治·贝尔，这一过程产生的涟漪会不可思议地、似乎偶然地从皇后区的阴影中蔓延到纽约州北部、弗吉尼亚州和佛罗里达州。

sentences.en: Dozens of people who never knew him, all cogs in the city's complicated machinery of mortality, would find themselves settling the affairs of an ordinary man
sentences.zh: 几十个从未认识他的人，作为城市复杂死亡机制中的齿轮，会发现自己正在处理一个普通人的身后事，

sentences.en: who left this world without anyone in particular noticing.
sentences.zh: 他离开这个世界时，并没有引起任何人的特别注意。

sentences.en: In discovering a death, you find a life story and perhaps meaning.
sentences.zh: 在发现死亡的过程中，你会发现一个人生故事，或许还有某种意义。

sentences.en: Could anything in the map of George Bell's existence have explained his lonely end?
sentences.zh: 乔治·贝尔存在轨迹中的任何东西能解释他孤独的结局吗？

sentences.en: Possibly not.
sentences.zh: 可能不能。

sentences.en: But it was true that George Bell died carrying some secrets.
sentences.zh: 但乔治·贝尔确实是带着一些秘密去世的。

sentences.en: Secrets about how he lived, and secrets about who mattered most to him.
sentences.zh: 关于他如何生活的秘密，以及关于谁对他最重要的人的秘密。

sentences.en: Those secrets would bring sorrow.
sentences.zh: 这些秘密会带来悲伤。

sentences.en: At the same time, they would deliver rewards.
sentences.zh: 同时，它们也会带来回报。

sentences.en: Death does that.
sentences.zh: 死亡就是这样。

sentences.en: It closes doors, but also opens them.
sentences.zh: 它关闭了门，但也打开了门。

sentences.en: Once firefighters had jimmied the door that July afternoon, the police squeezed into a beaten apartment, groaning with possessions, a grotesque parody of the lived-in condition.
sentences.zh: 那个七月的下午，消防员撬开门后，警察挤进了一间破旧的公寓，里面堆满了杂物，简直是对居住状态的一种怪诞讽刺。

sentences.en: Clearly, its occupant had been a hoarder.
sentences.zh: 显然，住户是个囤积狂。

sentences.en: The officers from the 115th precinct called the Medical Examiner's Office, which involves itself in suspicious deaths and unidentified bodies.
sentences.zh: 第115分局的警官致电法医办公室，该办公室负责处理可疑死亡和身份不明的尸体。

sentences.en: and a medical legal investigator arrived.
sentences.zh: 随后一名法医调查员抵达。

sentences.en: His task was to rule out foul play and look for evidence that could help locate the next of kin and identify the body.
sentences.zh: 他的任务是排除他杀，并寻找有助于寻找近亲和确认尸体身份的证据。

sentences.en: In short order, it was clear that nothing criminal had taken place.
sentences.zh: 很快，很明显没有发生任何犯罪行为。

sentences.en: No sign of force entry, bullet wounds, congealed blood.
sentences.zh: 没有强行闯入、枪伤或凝固血迹的迹象。

sentences.en: A fire department paramedic made the obvious pronouncement that the man was dead.
sentences.zh: 消防部门的一名护理人员做出了显而易见的宣告：该男子已经死亡。

sentences.en: Even a skeleton must be formally declared no longer living.
sentences.zh: 即使是一具骨架也必须被正式宣布不再存活。

sentences.en: The body was zipped into a human remains pouch.
sentences.zh: 尸体被装进了一个遗体袋中。

sentences.en: A transport team from the medical examiner's office drove it to the morgue at Queen's Hospital Center,
sentences.zh: 法医办公室的运输小组将其运往皇后医院中心的停尸房，

sentences.en: where it was deposited in one of some 100 refrigerated drawers, cooled to 35 degrees.
sentences.zh: 在那里，它被存放在约100个冷却至35华氏度的冷藏抽屉之一中。

sentences.en: It falls to the police to notify next of kin, but the neighbors did not know of any.
sentences.zh: 通知近亲是警察的职责，但邻居们不知道他有任何亲属。

sentences.en: Detectives grabbed some names and phone numbers from the apartment, called them, and got nothing.
sentences.zh: 侦探们从公寓里拿了一些名字和电话号码，打了过去，但一无所获。

sentences.en: The man had no wife, no siblings.
sentences.zh: 这名男子没有妻子，也没有兄弟姐妹。

sentences.en: The police estimate that they reached kin 85% of the time.
sentences.zh: 警方估计他们有85%的机会联系到亲属。

sentences.en: They struck out with George Bell.
sentences.zh: 但在乔治·贝尔身上，他们失败了。

sentences.en: At the Queen's morgue, identification personnel got started.
sentences.zh: 在皇后区停尸房，身份识别人员开始了工作。

sentences.en: Something like 90% of the corpses arriving at city morgues are identified by relatives or friends after they are shown photographs of the body.
sentences.zh: 城市停尸房接收的尸体中，约有90%是在向亲友展示尸体照片后被确认身份的。

sentences.en: Most remains depart from burial within a few days.
sentences.zh: 大多数遗体在几天内就会被送去安葬。

sentences.en: For the rest, it gets complicated.
sentences.zh: 对于其余的人，情况就变得复杂了。

sentences.en: The easiest resolution is furnished by fingerprints, otherwise by dental and medical records, or, as a last resort, by DNA.
sentences.zh: 最简单的解决方法是提供指纹，否则就通过牙科和医疗记录，或者作为最后手段，通过DNA。

sentences.en: The medical examiner can also do a so-called contextual ID.
sentences.zh: 法医也可以进行所谓的背景识别。

sentences.en: When all elements are considered, none of which by themselves bring certainty, a sort of circumstantial identification can be made.
sentences.zh: 当考虑到所有因素时，尽管它们本身都不能带来确定性，但可以做出一种间接的身份识别。

sentences.en: Fingerprints were taken, which required days because of the poor condition of the fingers.
sentences.zh: 提取了指纹，由于手指状况不佳，这花费了几天时间。

sentences.en: Enhanced techniques had to be used, such as soaking the fingers in a solution to soften them.
sentences.zh: 必须使用增强技术，例如将手指浸泡在溶液中使其软化。

sentences.en: The prints were sent to city, state, and federal databases.
sentences.zh: 指纹被发送到城市、州和联邦数据库。

sentences.en: No hits.
sentences.zh: 没有匹配结果。

sentences.en: Once nine days had elapsed and no next-of-kin had come forth, the medical examiner reported the death to the office of the Queens County Public Administrator,
sentences.zh: 九天过去了，仍没有近亲出现，法医将死讯报告给了皇后区公共行政官办公室，

sentences.en: an obscure agency that operates out of the state Supreme Court building in the Jamaica neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 这是一个在牙买加社区州最高法院大楼内运作的默默无闻的机构。

sentences.en: Its austere quarters are adjacent to Surrogates Court, familiarly known as Widows' and Orphans' Court, where wills are probated and battles are often waged over the dead.
sentences.zh: 其简朴的办公地点毗邻遗嘱认证法院，俗称“鳏寡孤独法院”，在那里进行遗嘱认证，并经常为死者遗产展开争夺。

sentences.en: Each county in New York City has a public administrator to manage estates When there is no one else to do so
sentences.zh: 纽约市每个区都有公共行政官来管理遗产，当没有其他人可以这样做时。

sentences.en: Most commonly when there is no will or no known heirs
sentences.zh: 最常见的情况是没有遗嘱或没有已知的继承人。

sentences.en: Public administrators tend to rouse attention
sentences.zh: 公共行政官往往会引起关注，

sentences.en: Only when complaints flare over their competence or their fees Or their tendency to oversee dens of political patronage
sentences.zh: 只有当人们对他们的能力或收费，或者他们监管政治恩惠窝点的倾向提出投诉时，

sentences.en: Or when they run afoul of the law
sentences.zh: 或者当他们触犯法律时。

sentences.en: Last year, a former longtime counsel to the Bronx County Public Administrator pleaded guilty to grand larceny,
sentences.zh: 去年，布朗克斯区公共行政官的一名前长期法律顾问承认犯有重大盗窃罪，

sentences.en: while a bookkeeper for the Kings County Public Administrator was sentenced to a prison term for stealing from the dead.
sentences.zh: 而国王区公共行政官的一名簿记员因从死者身上偷窃而被判入狱。

sentences.en: Recent audits by the city's controller found disturbing dysfunction at both of those offices, which the occupants said had been overstated.
sentences.zh: 市审计长最近的审计发现这两个办公室存在令人不安的功能失调，而相关人员称这些说法被夸大了。

sentences.en: The most recent audit of the Queen's office in 2012 raised no significant issues.
sentences.zh: 2012年对皇后区办公室的最近一次审计没有提出任何重大问题。

sentences.en: The Queen's unit employs 15 people and processes something like 1,500 deaths a year.
sentences.zh: 皇后区部门雇用了15人，每年处理约1500起死亡案件。

sentences.en: Appointed by the Queen's surrogate, Lois M.
sentences.zh: 由皇后区遗嘱认证法官任命，洛伊丝·M·

sentences.en: Rosenblatt, a lawyer, has been head of the office for the past 13 years.
sentences.zh: 罗森布拉特是一位律师，过去13年来一直担任该办公室的负责人。

sentences.en: Most cases arrive from nursing homes, others from the medical examiner, legal guardians, the police, undertakers.
sentences.zh: 大多数案件来自疗养院，其他来自法医、法定监护人、警察和殡仪馆。

sentences.en: While a majority of estates contain assets of less than $500, one had been worth $16 million.
sentences.zh: 虽然大多数遗产的资产不到500美元，但曾有一笔遗产价值1600万美元。

sentences.en: Meager estates can move swiftly.
sentences.zh: 微薄的遗产可以迅速处理。

sentences.en: Bigger ones routinely extend from 12 to 24 months.
sentences.zh: 较大的遗产通常需要12到24个月。

sentences.en: The office extracts a commission that starts at 5% of the first $100,000 of an estate and then slides downward, money that has entered into the city's general fund.
sentences.zh: 办公室提取的佣金从遗产前10万美元的5%开始，然后逐级递减，这些钱已进入城市的总基金。

sentences.en: An additional 1% goes toward the office's expenses.
sentences.zh: 额外的1%用于支付办公室的开支。

sentences.en: The office's counsel, who for 23 years has been Gerard Sweeney, a private lawyer who mainly does the public administrator's legal work, customarily gets a sliding legal fee
sentences.zh: 办公室的法律顾问杰拉德·斯威尼（Gerard Sweeney）担任此职已23年，他是一位主要处理公共行政官法律工作的私人律师，通常会获得一笔阶梯式法律费用，

sentences.en: that begins at 6% of the estate's first $750,000.
sentences.zh: 从遗产前75万美元的6%开始。

sentences.en: You can die in such anonymity in New York, he likes to say.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢说，在纽约，你可以死得如此默默无闻。

sentences.en: We've had instances of people dead for months.
sentences.zh: 我们遇到过有人死了好几个月的情况。

sentences.en: No one finds them.
sentences.zh: 没有人发现他们。

sentences.en: No one misses them.
sentences.zh: 没有人想念他们。

sentences.en: The man presumed to be George Bell joined the wash of cases, a fresh arrival that Ms. Rosenblatt viewed as nothing special at all.
sentences.zh: 被推定为乔治·贝尔的这名男子加入了案件的洪流，罗森布拉特女士认为这只是一个再普通不过的新案件。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the medical examiner needed records, x-rays would do, to confirm the identity of the body.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，法医需要记录，X光片也可以，以确认尸体的身份。

sentences.en: The office took its own chest x-rays, but still required earlier ones for comparison.
sentences.zh: 办公室拍摄了自己的胸部X光片，但仍需要之前的片子进行比对。

sentences.en: The medical examiner's office had no idea which doctors the man had seen, so in a Hail Mary maneuver, personnel began cold-calling hospitals and doctors in the vicinity
sentences.zh: 法医办公室不知道该男子看过哪些医生，因此在孤注一掷的情况下，工作人员开始向附近的医院和医生进行冷拨电话，

sentences.en: in a pattern that radiated outward from the Jackson Heights apartment.
sentences.zh: 以杰克逊高地的公寓为中心向外辐射。

sentences.en: Whoever picked up was asked if, by chance, George Bell had ever dropped in.
sentences.zh: 接电话的人都会被问到，乔治·贝尔是否碰巧来过。

sentences.en: Three investigators work for the Queens County Public Administrator.
sentences.zh: 皇后区公共行政官办公室有三名调查员。

sentences.en: They comb through the residences of the departed, mining their homes for clues as to what was owned, who their relatives were.
sentences.zh: 他们搜查死者的住所，挖掘他们家中的线索，以了解他们拥有什么，谁是他们的亲属。

sentences.en: It's a peculiar kind of work, seeing what strangers had kept in their closets, what they hung on the walls, what deodorant they liked.
sentences.zh: 这是一种奇特的工作，看看陌生人在壁橱里放了什么，墙上挂了什么，喜欢用什么除臭剂。

sentences.en: On July 24th, two investigators, Juan Plaza and Ronald Rodriguez, entered the glutted premises of the Bell apartment, clad in billowy hazmat suits and booties.
sentences.zh: 7月24日，两名调查员胡安·普拉扎和罗纳德·罗德里格斯穿着宽大的防护服和鞋套，进入了堆满杂物的贝尔公寓。

sentences.en: Investigators work in pairs to discourage theft.
sentences.zh: 调查员两人一组工作，以防盗窃。

sentences.en: Bleak as the place was, they had seen worse.
sentences.zh: 尽管这个地方很凄凉，但他们见过更糟的。

sentences.en: An apartment so swollen with belongings that the tenant, a woman, died standing up, unable to collapse to the floor.
sentences.zh: 公寓里堆满了杂物，租户——一位女性——死时仍保持着站立的姿势，无法倒在地板上。

sentences.en: or the place they fled swatting at swarms of fleas.
sentences.zh: 或者是他们逃离时，还在拍打着成群的跳蚤。

sentences.en: Yes, they saw a human existence that few others did.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们见证了极少数人才能看到的生命终局。

sentences.en: Mr. Plaza had been a data entry clerk before joining his macabre field in 1994.
sentences.zh: 普拉扎先生在1994年加入这个阴森的行业之前，曾是一名数据录入员。

sentences.en: Mr. Rodriguez had been a waiter and found his interest piqued in 2002.
sentences.zh: 罗德里格斯先生曾是一名服务员，他在2002年对这份工作产生了兴趣。

sentences.en: What qualified someone for the job?
sentences.zh: 什么样的人才有资格做这份工作？

sentences.en: Ms. Rosenblatt, the head of the office, summed it up.
sentences.zh: 办公室负责人罗森布拉特女士总结道。

sentences.en: People willing to go into these disgusting apartments.
sentences.zh: 愿意进入这些令人作呕的公寓的人。

sentences.en: The two men foraged through the unedited anarchy.
sentences.zh: 两人在未经整理的混乱中搜寻。

sentences.en: Eight hundred square feet, one bedroom.
sentences.zh: 八百平方英尺，一居室。

sentences.en: A stench thickened the air.
sentences.zh: 空气中弥漫着浓重的恶臭。

sentences.en: Mr. Plaza dabbed his nostrils with a Vicks vapor stick.
sentences.zh: 普拉扎先生用维克斯鼻通擦了擦鼻孔。

sentences.en: Mr. Rodriguez tufted out.
sentences.zh: 罗德里格斯先生走开了。

sentences.en: Vicks bothered his nose.
sentences.zh: 维克斯让他鼻子不舒服。

sentences.en: The only bed was the lumpy fold-out couch in the living room.
sentences.zh: 唯一的床是客厅里那张凹凸不平的折叠沙发。

sentences.en: The bedroom and bathroom looked pillaged.
sentences.zh: 卧室和浴室看起来像是被洗劫过一样。

sentences.en: The kitchen was splashed with trash and balled-up decades-old lottery tickets that had failed to deliver.
sentences.zh: 厨房里到处是垃圾，还有揉成团的、几十年前没中奖的彩票。

sentences.en: A soiled shopping list read,
sentences.zh: 一张弄脏的购物清单上写着：

sentences.en: Sea salt, garlic, carrots, broccoli, two-packs, TV Guide.
sentences.zh: 海盐、大蒜、胡萝卜、西兰花、两包装、电视指南。

sentences.en: The faucet didn't work.
sentences.zh: 水龙头坏了。

sentences.en: The chipped stove had no knobs and could not have been used to cook in a long time.
sentences.zh: 那台有缺口的炉子没有旋钮，显然很久没法用来做饭了。

sentences.en: The men scavenged for a will, a cemetery deed, financial documents, an address book, computer, cell phone, those sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 他们搜寻着遗嘱、墓地契约、财务文件、地址簿、电脑、手机之类的东西。

sentences.en: Photographs might show relatives.
sentences.zh: 照片或许能显示亲属信息。

sentences.en: Could that be a mom or sis beaming in that picture on the mantle?
sentences.zh: 壁炉架上照片里那个笑逐颜开的人，会是妈妈还是姐妹？

sentences.en: Portable objects of value were to be retrieved.
sentences.zh: 有价值的便携物品都要回收。

sentences.en: A Vermeer hangs on the wall?
sentences.zh: 墙上挂着维米尔的画？

sentences.en: Grab it.
sentences.zh: 拿走。

sentences.en: Once they found $30,000 in cash.
sentences.zh: 他们曾有一次发现了三万美元现金。

sentences.en: Another time, a Rolex wedged inside a radio.
sentences.zh: 还有一次，在收音机里塞了一块劳力士手表。

sentences.en: But the bar is not placed nearly that high.
sentences.zh: 但门槛并没有那么高。

sentences.en: In one instance, they lugged back a picture of the deceased in a Knights of Malta outfit.
sentences.zh: 有一次，他们搬回了一张死者身穿马耳他骑士团服装的照片。

sentences.en: In the slanting light, they scooped up papers from a table and some drawers in the living room.
sentences.zh: 在斜射的光线下，他们从客厅的桌子和抽屉里收集了文件。

sentences.en: They found $241 in bills and $187.45 in coins.
sentences.zh: 他们发现了241美元的纸币和187.45美元的硬币。

sentences.en: A silver relic watch did not look special, but they took it in case.
sentences.zh: 一块银色的旧手表看起来并不特别，但他们还是带走了，以防万一。

sentences.en: Fastened to the walls were a bear's head, steer horns, and some military pictures of planes and warships.
sentences.zh: 墙上挂着熊头、牛角，还有一些飞机和军舰的军事照片。

sentences.en: Over the couch hung a photo sequence of a parachutist coming in for a landing, with a certificate recording George Bell's first jump in 1963.
sentences.zh: 沙发上方挂着一组跳伞运动员着陆的照片，还有一张记录乔治·贝尔1963年首次跳伞的证书。

sentences.en: Chinese food cartons and pizza boxes were ubiquitous.
sentences.zh: 中餐外卖盒和披萨盒随处可见。

sentences.en: Shelves were stacked with music tapes and videos,
sentences.zh: 架子上堆满了音乐磁带和录像带，

sentences.en: Top Gun, Braveheart, Yule Log.
sentences.zh: 《壮志凌云》、《勇敢的心》、《圣诞壁炉》。

sentences.en: A splouched calendar from Lucky Market hung in the bathroom, flipped open to August 2007.
sentences.zh: 浴室里挂着一本来自幸运市场的污损日历，翻在2007年8月那一页。

sentences.en: Hoarding is deemed a mental disorder, poorly understood, that stirs people to incoherent acts.
sentences.zh: 囤积症被认为是一种心理障碍，人们对其了解甚少，它会驱使人做出不连贯的行为。

sentences.en: Sufferers may buy products simply to have them.
sentences.zh: 患者可能会仅仅为了拥有而购买商品。

sentences.en: Amid the mess were a half-dozen unopened ironing board covers, multiple packages of unused Christmas lights, four new tire pressure gauges.
sentences.zh: 在杂物中，有六个未开封的熨衣板套、多包未使用的圣诞灯串、四个全新的胎压计。

sentences.en: The investigators returned twice more, rounding up more papers, another $95.
sentences.zh: 调查员又回去两次，收集了更多文件，又发现了95美元。

sentences.en: They found no cell phone, no computer or credit cards.
sentences.zh: 他们没有找到手机、电脑或信用卡。

sentences.en: Rummaging through the personal effects of the dead, sensing the misery in these rooms can color your thoughts.
sentences.zh: 翻阅死者的私人物品，感受这些房间里的悲惨，会影响你的思绪。

sentences.en: The work changes people, and it has changed these men.
sentences.zh: 这份工作改变了人，也改变了这两个人。

sentences.en: Mr. Rodriguez, 57 and divorced, has a greater sense of urgency
sentences.zh: 57岁且离异的罗德里格斯先生，有了更强的紧迫感。

sentences.en: I try to build a life like it's the last day, he said You never know when you will die
sentences.zh: 他说：我试着像过最后一天一样去生活，你永远不知道自己什么时候会死。

sentences.en: Before this I went along like I would live forever
sentences.zh: 在此之前，我一直以为自己会长生不老。

sentences.en: The solitude of so many deaths wears on Mr. Plaza
sentences.zh: 这么多死亡带来的孤独感让普拉扎先生感到沉重。

sentences.en: The fear that someday it will be him splayed on the floor in one of these silent apartments
sentences.zh: 他担心有一天，自己也会像这样瘫倒在这些寂静公寓的地板上。

sentences.en: This job teaches you a lot, he said
sentences.zh: 他说，这份工作教会了你很多。

sentences.en: You learn whatever material stuff you have, you should use it and share it.
sentences.zh: 你学会了无论你拥有什么物质财富，都应该去使用它、分享它。

sentences.en: Share yourself.
sentences.zh: 分享你自己。

sentences.en: People die with nobody to talk to.
sentences.zh: 人们死的时候，身边连个说话的人都没有。

sentences.en: They die and relatives come out of the woodwork.
sentences.zh: 他们死了，亲戚们就从各个角落冒了出来。

sentences.en: He was my uncle.
sentences.zh: 他是我叔叔。

sentences.en: He was my cousin.
sentences.zh: 他是我表亲。

sentences.en: Give me what he had.
sentences.zh: 把他留下的东西给我。

sentences.en: Gimme, gimme.
sentences.zh: 给我，给我。

sentences.en: Yet when he was alive, they never visited, never knew the person.
sentences.zh: 然而当他活着的时候，他们从不探望，甚至根本不认识这个人。

sentences.en: From working in this office, my life changed.
sentences.zh: 在这间办公室工作，改变了我的生活。

sentences.en: He is 52.
sentences.zh: 他今年52岁。

sentences.en: Also divorced and without children.
sentences.zh: 同样离异，没有孩子。

sentences.en: But he keeps expanding his base of friends.
sentences.zh: 但他不断扩大自己的朋友圈。

sentences.en: Every day, he sends them motivational Instagram messages.
sentences.zh: 每天，他都会给他们发送励志的Instagram消息。

sentences.en: With each sunrise, may we value every minute.
sentences.zh: 愿我们珍惜每一个日出后的时光。

sentences.en: Be kind, smile to the world, and it will smile back.
sentences.zh: 善良一点，对世界微笑，世界也会报以微笑。

sentences.en: Share your life with loved ones.
sentences.zh: 与所爱之人分享你的生活。

sentences.en: Love, forgive, forget.
sentences.zh: 去爱，去宽恕，去遗忘。

sentences.en: yet.
sentences.zh: 然而。

sentences.en: He said, when I die, someone will find out the same day or the next day.
sentences.zh: 他说，当我死的时候，有人会在当天或第二天发现。

sentences.en: Since I've worked here, my list of friends has gotten longer and longer.
sentences.zh: 自从我在这里工作，我的朋友名单变得越来越长。

sentences.en: I don't want to die alone.
sentences.zh: 我不想孤独地死去。

sentences.en: In his queen's cubicle, wearing rubber gloves, Patrick Stressler thumbed through the sheaf of documents retrieved by the two investigators.
sentences.zh: 在属于他的小隔间里，帕特里克·斯特雷斯勒戴着橡胶手套，翻阅着两名调查员取回的文件。

sentences.en: Mr. Stressler, the caseworker with the public administrator's office responsible for piecing together George Bell's estate, is formerly a decedent property
sentences.zh: 斯特雷斯勒先生是公共行政办公室负责整理乔治·贝尔遗产的个案工作者，他曾是一名遗产财产

sentences.en: agent, a title he finds useful as a conversation starter at parties.
sentences.zh: 代理人，这个头衔他觉得在聚会上是个很好的开场白。

sentences.en: He is 27 and had been a restaurant cashier five years ago when he learned you could be a decedent property agent and became one.
sentences.zh: 他今年27岁，五年前还是餐厅收银员，当他得知可以成为遗产财产代理人时，就入行了。

sentences.en: He began with the pictures.
sentences.zh: 他从照片开始看起。

sentences.en: Mr. Stressler mingles in the leavings of people he can never meet and especially likes to ponder the photographs, so you get a sense of a person's history, not that they just died.
sentences.zh: 斯特雷斯勒先生在那些他永远无法谋面之人的遗物中穿梭，他特别喜欢琢磨这些照片，这样你就能感受到一个人的历史，而不仅仅是他们已经去世的事实。

sentences.en: The snapshots ranged over the humdrum of life.
sentences.zh: 这些快照记录了生活的琐碎。

sentences.en: A child wearing a holster and toy pistols.
sentences.zh: 一个戴着枪套和玩具手枪的孩子。

sentences.en: A man in military dress.
sentences.zh: 一个身穿军装的男人。

sentences.en: Men fishing.
sentences.zh: 钓鱼的男人们。

sentences.en: A young woman sitting on a chair in a corner.
sentences.zh: 一个坐在角落椅子上的年轻女子。

sentences.en: A high school class on a stage, everyone wearing blackface.
sentences.zh: 舞台上的一届高中班级，每个人都涂着黑脸。

sentences.en: Different times, Mr. Stressler mused.
sentences.zh: 不同的时代，斯特雷斯勒沉思道。

sentences.en: In the end, the photos divulged little of what George Bell had done across his 72 years.
sentences.zh: 最终，这些照片几乎没能揭示乔治·贝尔72年来做过什么。

sentences.en: The thicket of papers yielded a few hazy colonels, an unused passport issued in
sentences.zh: 那一堆文件中只发现了一些模糊的军衔，还有一本未使用的护照，签发于

sentences.en: 2007 to George Main Bell, Jr., showing a thick-necked man with a meaty face ripened by time, born January 15, 1942.
sentences.zh: 2007年，持有人是乔治·梅恩·贝尔二世，照片上是一个脖子粗壮、脸庞饱经风霜的男人，出生于1942年1月15日。

sentences.en: Documents establishing that his father, George Bell, died in 1969 at 59.
sentences.zh: 文件证明他的父亲乔治·贝尔于1969年去世，享年59岁。

sentences.en: His mother, Davina Bell, in 1981 at 76.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲达维娜·贝尔于1981年去世，享年76岁。

sentences.en: Some holiday cards.
sentences.zh: 一些节日贺卡。

sentences.en: Several from an L.C.
sentences.zh: 几张来自新泽西州雷德班克的L.C.

sentences.en: Logan in Red Bank, New Jersey, thanking him for gifts of Godiva chocolates.
sentences.zh: 洛根，感谢他赠送的高迪瓦巧克力。

sentences.en: One dated 2001 said, I called Sunday around 2.
sentences.zh: 一张2001年的贺卡写道：我周日两点左右打过电话。

sentences.en: No answer.
sentences.zh: 没人接。

sentences.en: We'll try again.
sentences.zh: 我们再试一次。

sentences.en: A 2007 Thanksgiving Day card read,
sentences.zh: 一张2007年的感恩节贺卡写着：

sentences.en: I have been trying to call you, but no answer.
sentences.zh: 我一直试着给你打电话，但没人接。

sentences.en: A 2001 Christmas card signed,
sentences.zh: 一张2001年的圣诞贺卡上写着：

sentences.en: Love Always, Eleanor.
sentences.zh: 永远爱你的，埃莉诺。

sentences.en: Poffy.
sentences.zh: 波菲。

sentences.en: With the message,
sentences.zh: 附言写道：

sentences.en: I seldom mention it, but I hope you realize how much it means to have you for a friend.
sentences.zh: 我很少提起，但我希望你明白，能有你这样的朋友对我来说意味着什么。

sentences.en: I care a lot for you.
sentences.zh: 我很在乎你。

sentences.en: Cards from a Thomas Higginbotham, addressed to Big George and signed Friend Tom.
sentences.zh: 来自托马斯·希金博瑟姆的贺卡，称呼他为“大乔治”，署名为“朋友汤姆”。

sentences.en: A golden find, H&R Block-Prepared Tax Returns, useful for divining assets.
sentences.zh: 一个重大的发现：H&R Block准备的纳税申报表，对于推算资产很有用。

sentences.en: The latest showed adjusted gross income of $13,207 from a pension and interest, another $21,311 from Social Security.
sentences.zh: 最新的一份显示，调整后总收入为13,207美元，来自养老金和利息，另有21,311美元来自社会保障金。

sentences.en: The bank statements contained the biggest revelation.
sentences.zh: 银行对账单包含了最大的发现。

sentences.en: For what appeared to be a simple life, they showed balances of several hundred thousand dollars.
sentences.zh: 对于一个看起来生活简单的人来说，账单显示余额高达几十万美元。

sentences.en: Letters went out to confirm the amounts.
sentences.zh: 信件已发出以确认金额。

sentences.en: No evidence of stocks or bonds, but a small life insurance policy with the beneficiaries, his parents.
sentences.zh: 没有股票或债券的证据，但有一份小额人寿保险，受益人是他的父母。

sentences.en: And there was a will dated 1982.

sentences.en: His life began small and plain.

sentences.en: George Bell was especially attached to his parents,
sentences.zh: 乔治·贝尔特别依恋他的父母，

sentences.en: He slept on the pull-out sofa in the living room while his parents claimed the bedroom, and he continued to sleep there even after they died.
sentences.zh: 他睡在客厅的折叠沙发上，而父母住卧室，即使在他们去世后，他依然睡在那里。

sentences.en: Both parents came from Scotland.
sentences.zh: 他的父母都来自苏格兰。

sentences.en: His father was a tool and dye machinist, and his mother worked for a time as a seamstress in the toy industry.
sentences.zh: 他父亲是一名模具机械师，母亲曾一度在玩具行业做缝纫工。

sentences.en: After high school, he joined his father as an apprentice.
sentences.zh: 高中毕业后，他跟随父亲做了学徒。

sentences.en: In 1961, he made an acquaintance at a local bar, a moving man.
sentences.zh: 1961年，他在当地一家酒吧结识了一位搬家工人。

sentences.en: They became friends, and the moving man pulled George Bell into the moving business.
sentences.zh: 他们成了朋友，这位搬家工人把乔治·贝尔拉进了搬家行业。

sentences.en: His name was Tom Higginbotham.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫汤姆·希金博瑟姆。

sentences.en: Three fellow movers also became friends, Frank Mersey, Albert Schober, and Martin Westbrook, the men in the will.
sentences.zh: 另外三位搬家同事也成了朋友，分别是弗兰克·默西、阿尔伯特·肖伯和马丁·韦斯特布鲁克，也就是遗嘱中的那些人。

sentences.en: They mainly moved business offices, and they all guzzled booze in titanic proportions.
sentences.zh: 他们主要搬运商业办公室，而且所有人都酗酒成性。

sentences.en: We were a bunch of drunks, Mr. Westbrook said.
sentences.zh: 我们是一群酒鬼，韦斯特布鲁克先生说。

sentences.en: I'm a juicer, but George put me to shame.
sentences.zh: 我是个酒鬼，但乔治让我自愧不如。

sentences.en: He was a real nice guy, kind of a hermit.
sentences.zh: 他是个很好的人，有点像个隐士。

sentences.en: Boy, we had some good times.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我们度过了一些美好的时光。

sentences.en: In the words of Mr. Higginbotham,
sentences.zh: 用希金博瑟姆先生的话说，

sentences.en: We were great friends.
sentences.zh: 我们是好朋友。

sentences.en: I don't know if you can say it this way, but we were men who loved each other.
sentences.zh: 我不知道能不能这么说，但我们是彼此相爱的男人。

sentences.en: They called him Big George, for he was a thick-set, brawny man, weighing perhaps 210 pounds.
sentences.zh: 他们叫他“大乔治”，因为他是一个身材魁梧、肌肉发达的男人，体重可能达到210磅。

sentences.en: Later, his ravenous appetite had him pushing 350.
sentences.zh: 后来，他贪婪的食欲让他体重直逼350磅。

sentences.en: He had a puckish streak.
sentences.zh: 他有一种顽皮的性格。

sentences.en: Once a woman invited him and Mr. Higginbotham to a party at her parents' house.
sentences.zh: 有一次，一位女士邀请他和希金博瑟姆先生去她父母家参加聚会。

sentences.en: Her father kept tropical fish.
sentences.zh: 她父亲养了热带鱼。

sentences.en: She showed George Bell the tank.
sentences.zh: 她向乔治·贝尔展示了鱼缸。

sentences.en: When he admired a distinctive fish, she said,
sentences.zh: 当他赞美一条独特的鱼时，她说，

sentences.en: Oh, that's an expensive one.
sentences.zh: 哦，那条很贵。

sentences.en: He picked up a net, caught the fish, and swallowed it.
sentences.zh: 他拿起网，抓起那条鱼，把它吞了下去。

sentences.en: One day, the friends were moving a financial firm.
sentences.zh: 有一天，朋友们正在为一家金融公司搬家。

sentences.en: After they had fitted the desks into the new offices,
sentences.zh: 在他们把办公桌安装进新办公室后，

sentences.en: George Bell slid notes into the drawers, writing things like,
sentences.zh: 乔治·贝尔把纸条塞进抽屉里，写着诸如：

sentences.en: I'm madly in love with you.
sentences.zh: 我疯狂地爱着你。

sentences.en: Meet me at the water cooler.
sentences.zh: 在饮水机旁见。

sentences.en: Or,
sentences.zh: 或者，

sentences.en: There's a bomb under your chair.
sentences.zh: 你的椅子下面有炸弹。

sentences.en: Your next move might be your laSt.
sentences.zh: 你的下一步行动可能是你最后一步。

sentences.en: Dumb pranks.
sentences.zh: 愚蠢的恶作剧。

sentences.en: Big George being Big George.
sentences.zh: 大乔治就是大乔治。

sentences.en: Friends, though, found him difficult to crack open.
sentences.zh: 然而，朋友们发现他很难敞开心扉。

sentences.en: There were things inside no one could get out.
sentences.zh: 他内心深处有一些东西是没人能触及的。

sentences.en: You learned to suppress your questions around him.
sentences.zh: 你学会了在他身边压抑自己的好奇心。

sentences.en: He had his burdens.
sentences.zh: 他有自己的负担。

sentences.en: His father died young.
sentences.zh: 他父亲英年早逝。

sentences.en: As she aged, his mother became crippled by arthritis.
sentences.zh: 随着年龄增长，他母亲因关节炎而残疾。

sentences.en: He cared for her, fetching her food and bathing her until her death.
sentences.zh: 他照顾她，为她取食物并为她洗澡，直到她去世。

sentences.en: He was fastidious about his money, only trusted banks for his savings.
sentences.zh: 他对钱很谨慎，只信任银行来存钱。

sentences.en: There was a woman he began dating when she was 19 and he was 25.
sentences.zh: 他曾与一位女性开始交往，当时她19岁，他25岁。

sentences.en: We got real keen on each other, she said later.
sentences.zh: 我们当时非常喜欢对方，她后来回忆道。

sentences.en: He made me feel special.
sentences.zh: 他让我感觉自己很特别。

sentences.en: The marriage was planned.
sentences.zh: 婚事已经计划好了。

sentences.en: They spoke to a wedding hall.
sentences.zh: 他们联系了婚礼大厅。

sentences.en: He bought a suit.
sentences.zh: 他买了一套西装。

sentences.en: Then, he told friends, the woman's mother had wanted him to sign a prenuptial agreement to protect her daughter if the marriage should break apart.
sentences.zh: 然后，他告诉朋友，女方的母亲想让他签署一份婚前协议，以便在婚姻破裂时保护她的女儿。

sentences.en: He ended the engagement and never had another serious relationship.
sentences.zh: 他结束了订婚，此后再也没有过认真的感情。

sentences.en: That woman was Eleanor Albert, the fourth name in the will.
sentences.zh: 那位女士就是埃莉诺·阿尔伯特，遗嘱中的第四个名字。

sentences.en: Some years later, she married an older man who made equipment for a party supply company and moved upstate to become Ms. Phlegm.
sentences.zh: 几年后，她嫁给了一位为派对用品公司制造设备的年长男子，并搬到北部，成了弗莱姆女士。

sentences.en: In 2002, her husband died.
sentences.zh: 2002年，她的丈夫去世了。

sentences.en: Distance and time never dampened the emotional affinity between her and George Bell.
sentences.zh: 距离和时间从未冲淡她与乔治·贝尔之间的情感亲近感。

sentences.en: They spoke on the phone and exchanged cards.
sentences.zh: 他们通过电话，并交换贺卡。

sentences.en: We had something for each other that never got used up, she said.
sentences.zh: 我们对彼此有一种从未耗尽的情感，她说。

sentences.en: She had sent him a Valentine's Day card just last year.
sentences.zh: 就在去年，她还给他寄过一张情人节贺卡。

sentences.en: George, think of you often with love.
sentences.zh: 乔治，经常带着爱意想起你。

sentences.en: And unbeknownst to her, he had put her in his will and kept her there.
sentences.zh: 而她不知道的是，他已经把她写进了遗嘱，并一直保留着。

sentences.en: Her life finished up a lot like his.
sentences.zh: 她的人生结局和他很像。

sentences.en: She lived alone in a trailer.
sentences.zh: 她独自住在一辆拖车里。

sentences.en: She died of a heart attack.
sentences.zh: 她死于心脏病发作。

sentences.en: A neighbor who cleared her snow found her.
sentences.zh: 一位帮她清理积雪的邻居发现了她。

sentences.en: She had gotten obese.
sentences.zh: 她变得肥胖了。

sentences.en: Her brother had her cremated.
sentences.zh: 她的兄弟为她进行了火化。

sentences.en: A difference was that she left behind debt owed to the bank and to credit card companies.
sentences.zh: 不同之处在于，她留下了一些欠银行和信用卡公司的债务。

sentences.en: All that she would pass on was tens of thousands of dollars of George Bell's money, money that she never got to touch.
sentences.zh: 她能留下的全部就是乔治·贝尔留下的数万美元，那是她从未触碰过的钱。

sentences.en: Some would filter down to her brother who had no plans for it.
sentences.zh: 一些钱会流向她那对此毫无计划的兄弟。

sentences.en: A slice went to Michael Garber, her nephew, who drives a bus at Disney
sentences.zh: 一部分给了迈克尔·加伯，她的侄子，他在迪士尼世界开巴士。

sentences.en: World.
sentences.zh: 世界。

sentences.en: A friend of his aunt's had owned a Camaro convertible that she relished, and he might buy a used Camaro in her honor.
sentences.zh: 他姑妈的一位朋友曾拥有一辆她非常喜欢的科迈罗敞篷车，他可能会为了纪念她买一辆二手的科迈罗。

sentences.en: Some more would go to Sarah Tata, a niece, retired and living in
sentences.zh: 还有一些会给莎拉·塔塔，一位侄女，退休后住在佛罗里达州的阿尔塔蒙特斯普林斯，她打算把钱存起来以备不时之需。

sentences.en: Altamont Springs, Florida, who plans to save it for a rainy day.
sentences.zh: 你总是听说你不认识的人去世并给你留钱，她说。

sentences.en: You always hear about people you don't know dying and leaving you money, she said.
sentences.zh: 我从没想过这种事会发生在我身上。

sentences.en: I never thought it would happen to me.
sentences.zh: 还有一些会流向埃莉诺·弗莱姆的另一位侄女多萝西·加德纳，一位退休的服务员和家庭护理助理。

sentences.en: And some would funnel down to Eleanor Flem's other niece, Dorothy Gardner, a retired waitress and home health care aide.
sentences.zh: 她住在佛罗里达州的阿波普卡。

sentences.en: She lives in Apopka, Florida.
sentences.zh: 从没听说过乔治·贝尔。

sentences.en: Never heard of George Bell.
sentences.zh: 她战胜了两次癌症，还有几千美元的医疗费可能终于可以还清了。

sentences.en: She has survived two cancers and has several thousand dollars in medical bills that could finally disappear.
sentences.zh: 我一直在尽我所能每月还25美元，她说。

sentences.en: I've been paying off $25 a month, what I can, she said.
sentences.zh: 我从没想过会发生这种事。

sentences.en: I never would have expected this.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: It's crazy.
sentences.zh: 1996年，乔治·贝尔在搬家工作中抬桌子时伤了左肩和脊椎，他的人生发生了改变。

sentences.en: In 1996, George Bell hurt his left shoulder and spine lifting a desk on a moving job and his life took a different shape.
sentences.zh: 他获得了工伤赔偿和社会保障残疾津贴的批准，并开始领取卡车司机工会的养老金。

sentences.en: He received approval for workers' compensation and social security disability payments and began collecting a pension from the Teamsters.
sentences.zh: 尽管他再也没有工作过。

sentences.en: Though he never worked again.
sentences.zh: 他拥有他所需要的所有收入。

sentences.en: He had all the income he needed.
sentences.zh: 他过去常请朋友们过来一起看电视，还会为他们做饭。

sentences.en: He used to have buddies over to watch television, and he would cook for them.
sentences.zh: 后来他不再请任何人过来了。

sentences.en: Then he stopped having anyone over.
sentences.zh: 没人知道为什么。

sentences.en: No one knew why.
sentences.zh: 老朋友们渐行渐远，随之而去的是乔治·贝尔生命中曾经的一些活力。

sentences.en: Old friends had drifted away, and with them some of the fire in George Bell's life.
sentences.zh: 在他的搬家同事中，默西先生于1994年退休，2011年去世。

sentences.en: Of his moving man colleagues, Mr. Mersey retired in 1994 and died in 2011.
sentences.zh: 肖伯先生于1996年退休并搬到布鲁克林，失去了联系，他于2002年去世。

sentences.en: Mr. Schober retired in 1996 and moved to Brooklyn, losing touch He died in 2002
sentences.zh: 希金博瑟姆先生于1973年辞去了搬家工作，搬到北部，为州政府担任环境科学家。

sentences.en: Mr. Higginbotham quit the moving business and moved upstate in 1973 to work for the state as an environmental scientist
sentences.zh: 他的人生轨迹从此不同。

sentences.en: He is now 74, retired and living alone in Virginia
sentences.zh: 他今年74岁，已退休，独自住在弗吉尼亚州。

sentences.en: The last time he spoke to George Bell was 10 years ago
sentences.zh: 他最后一次和乔治·贝尔通话是在10年前。

sentences.en: He used a code of ringing and hanging up to get him to answer his phone, but in time he got no answer.
sentences.zh: 他曾用一种“响一声就挂断”的暗号让他接电话，但后来就再也没人接了。

sentences.en: He sent cards, beseeched him to come and visit, but he wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 他寄过贺卡，恳求他来探望，但他从不答应。

sentences.en: It was two months before Mr. Higginbotham found out George Bell had died.
sentences.zh: 直到乔治·贝尔去世两个月后，希金博瑟姆先生才得知消息。

sentences.en: It has been hard for him to reconcile the way George Bell's money came to him.
sentences.zh: 对于乔治·贝尔留给他的这笔钱，他一直难以释怀。

sentences.en: I've been stressed about this, he said.
sentences.zh: “我为此感到压力很大，”他说。

sentences.en: I haven't been sleeping.
sentences.zh: “我一直睡不好觉。”

sentences.en: My stomach hurts.
sentences.zh: “胃也疼。”

sentences.en: My blood pressure is up.
sentences.zh: “血压也升高了。”

sentences.en: I argued with him time and again to get out of that apartment and spend his money and enjoy life.
sentences.zh: “我一次又一次地劝他搬出那间公寓，把钱花掉，享受生活。”

sentences.en: I sent him so many brochures on places to go, I thought I understood George.
sentences.zh: “我寄给他那么多旅游手册，我以为我很了解乔治。”

sentences.en: Now I realize I didn't understand him at all.
sentences.zh: “现在我才意识到，我根本一点都不了解他。”

sentences.en: Mr. Higginbotham was content with the fundaments of his own life, his modest one-bedroom apartment, his 15-year-old truck.
sentences.zh: 希金博瑟姆先生对自己的生活现状很满足，他住在一间简朴的一居室公寓里，开着一辆15年车龄的卡车。

sentences.en: He put the inheritance into mutual funds and figures it will help his three grandchildren through college.
sentences.zh: 他把这笔遗产存进了共同基金，打算用它来资助三个孙辈上大学。

sentences.en: George Bell's Money, Educating the Future
sentences.zh: 乔治·贝尔的钱，教育的未来

sentences.en: In 1994, Mr. Westbrook hurt his knee and left the moving business.
sentences.zh: 1994年，韦斯特布鲁克先生膝盖受伤，离开了搬家行业。

sentences.en: He moved to Spraker's, where he had a cattle farm.
sentences.zh: 他搬到了斯普雷克，在那里经营一个养牛场。

sentences.en: When he got older and his marriage dissolved, he sold the farm but still lives nearby.
sentences.zh: 后来他年纪大了，婚姻也破裂了，便卖掉了农场，但仍住在附近。

sentences.en: He is 74.
sentences.zh: 他今年74岁。

sentences.en: It was several years ago that he last spoke to George Bell on the phone.
sentences.zh: 那是几年前，他最后一次在电话里和乔治·贝尔交谈。

sentences.en: Mr. Bell told him he did not get out much.
sentences.zh: 贝尔先生告诉他，他不怎么出门。

sentences.en: He has three grandchildren and wants to move to a mellower climate.
sentences.zh: 他有三个孙辈，想搬到一个气候更宜人的地方。

sentences.en: He plans to give some of the money to Mr. Mersey's widow because Mr. Mersey had been his best friend.
sentences.zh: 他打算把一部分钱给默西先生的遗孀，因为默西先生曾是他最好的朋友。

sentences.en: My sister needs some dental work, he said.
sentences.zh: “我妹妹需要看牙医，”他说。

sentences.en: I need some dental work.
sentences.zh: “我也需要看牙医。”

sentences.en: I need hearing aids.
sentences.zh: “我还需要助听器。”

sentences.en: The golden age ain't so cheap.
sentences.zh: “黄金时代过得可不便宜。”

sentences.en: Big George's money will make my old age easier.
sentences.zh: “大乔治的钱会让我的晚年生活轻松些。”

sentences.en: He felt awful about his dying alone, nobody knowing.
sentences.zh: 他为乔治孤独死去、无人知晓而感到难过。

sentences.en: Yeah, that'll happen to me, he said.
sentences.zh: “是啊，我也可能会那样，”他说。

sentences.en: I'm a loner too.
sentences.zh: “我也是个独来独往的人。”

sentences.en: There's maybe four or five people up here I talk to.
sentences.zh: “在这儿我能说上话的也就四五个人。”

sentences.en: In his final years, with the moving man gone,
sentences.zh: 在他生命的最后几年里，随着搬家工人的离去，

sentences.en: George Bell's life had become emptier.
sentences.zh: 乔治·贝尔的生活变得更加空虚。

sentences.en: Neighbors nodded to him on the street, and he smiled.
sentences.zh: 邻居们在街上向他点头致意，他也会报以微笑。

sentences.en: He told lively stories to the young woman next door who lived with her parents when he bumped into her.
sentences.zh: 当他偶遇隔壁那位和父母住在一起的年轻姑娘时，他会给她讲些生动的故事。

sentences.en: She recently became a police officer, and she was the one who had smelled what she knew was death.
sentences.zh: 她最近成为了一名警察，正是她闻到了那股她所熟悉的死亡气息。

sentences.en: But in the end, George Bell seemed to keep just one true friend.
sentences.zh: 但最终，乔治·贝尔似乎只留下了一个真正的朋友。

sentences.en: He had been a fixture at a neighborhood pub called Bud's Bar.
sentences.zh: 他曾是附近一家叫“巴德酒吧”的常客。

sentences.en: He showed up in his cut-off blue sweatshirt so often that some regulars called him Sweatshirt Bell.
sentences.zh: 他总是穿着那件剪掉袖口的蓝色运动衫出现，以至于一些常客叫他“运动衫贝尔”。

sentences.en: At one point, he eased up on his drinking, then, worried about his health, quit.
sentences.zh: 有段时间，他减少了饮酒，后来又因为担心健康而彻底戒了。

sentences.en: But he still went to Bud's, ordering club soda.
sentences.zh: 但他还是会去巴德酒吧，点一杯苏打水。

sentences.en: In April 2005, Bud's closed.
sentences.zh: 2005年4月，巴德酒吧关门了。

sentences.en: Many regulars gravitated to another bar, Legends.
sentences.zh: 许多常客转而去了另一家酒吧——传奇酒吧。

sentences.en: George Bell went a few times, then transferred his allegiance to Bantry Bay Public House in Long Island City.
sentences.zh: 乔治·贝尔去了几次，然后把阵地转移到了长岛市的班特里湾酒吧。

sentences.en: He would meet his friend there.
sentences.zh: 他会在那里见他的朋友。

sentences.en: The sign of the entrance to Bantry Bay says,
sentences.zh: 班特里湾酒吧入口处的招牌上写着：

sentences.en: Enter as strangers, leave as friends.
sentences.zh: “以陌生人身份进入，以朋友身份离开。”

sentences.en: Squished in near the window was Frank Bertone, sipping soup and nursing a drink.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克·贝尔托内挤在窗边，喝着汤，手里端着一杯酒。

sentences.en: He is known as the Dude,
sentences.zh: 他被称为“老兄”，

sentences.en: George Bell's last good friend.
sentences.zh: 是乔治·贝尔最后的好友。

sentences.en: In the early 1980s, not long after moving to Jackson Heights, he stopped in at Bud's in need of a restroom.
sentences.zh: 20世纪80年代初，他刚搬到杰克逊高地不久，因为想借用洗手间而走进了巴德酒吧。

sentences.en: A big man had bellowed,
sentences.zh: 一个大块头大声喊道：

sentences.en: Have a beer!
sentences.zh: “来杯啤酒！”

sentences.en: That was George Bell.
sentences.zh: 那个人就是乔治·贝尔。

sentences.en: In time, a friendship was spawned, deepening during the 15 years that remained of George Bell's life.
sentences.zh: 久而久之，一段友谊由此萌生，并在乔治·贝尔生命的最后15年里愈发深厚。

sentences.en: They met on Saturdays at Bantry Bay.
sentences.zh: 他们每周六在班特里湾酒吧见面。

sentences.en: They fished in the Rockaways and at Jones Beach, sometimes with others.
sentences.zh: 他们有时会和别人一起去洛克威和琼斯海滩钓鱼。

sentences.en: Mr. Bell bought a car to get out to the good spots, but the car otherwise mostly sat.
sentences.zh: 贝尔先生买了一辆车去那些好地方，但平时车大多都闲置着。

sentences.en: They passed time meandering around, the days bleeding into one another.
sentences.zh: 他们漫无目的地消磨时光，日子一天天过去。

sentences.en: Where did we go?
sentences.zh: “我们去哪儿了？”

sentences.en: Mr. Bertone said.
sentences.zh: 贝尔托内先生说。

sentences.en: No place.
sentences.zh: “哪儿也没去。”

sentences.en: One time we sat for hours in the parking lot of Bed Bath & Beyond.
sentences.zh: “有一次我们在‘家居博览’的停车场坐了好几个小时。”

sentences.en: What did we talk about?
sentences.zh: “我们聊了些什么？”

sentences.en: The world's probleMs.
sentences.zh: “世界难题。”

sentences.en: Just like that, the two of us solved the world's probleMs.
sentences.zh: “就这样，我们俩解决了世界难题。”

sentences.en: Mr. Bertone is 67, a retired inspector for Consolidated Edison.
sentences.zh: 贝尔托内先生今年67岁，是联合爱迪生公司的退休检查员。

sentences.en: Over the last decade, he had spent more time with George Bell than anyone.
sentences.zh: 在过去的十年里，他比任何人都花更多时间陪伴乔治·贝尔。

sentences.en: But he didn't feel he truly knew him.
sentences.zh: 但他并不觉得他真正了解他。

sentences.en: One thing about George is, he didn't get personal, he said.
sentences.zh: “乔治有一点就是，他不谈私事，”他说。

sentences.en: Not ever.
sentences.zh: “从来不谈。”

sentences.en: He knew he had never married.
sentences.zh: 他知道他从未结过婚。

sentences.en: He spoke of girlfriends, but Mr. Bertone never met any.
sentences.zh: 他提到过女朋友，但贝尔托内先生从未见过任何一个。

sentences.en: The two had even swapped views on wills and what happens to your money in the end, though Mr. Bertone did not know George Bell had drafted a will before they met.
sentences.zh: 两人甚至交流过关于遗嘱以及钱财最终归属的看法，尽管贝尔托内先生并不知道乔治·贝尔在他们相识之前就已经立好了遗嘱。

sentences.en: Mr. Bertone would invite him to his place, but he would beg off.
sentences.zh: 贝尔托内先生曾邀请他去家里，但他总是推辞。

sentences.en: George Bell never had him over.
sentences.zh: 乔治·贝尔从未邀请过他去家里。

sentences.en: Once, some eight years ago, Mr. Bertone trooped out there when he hadn't heard from him in a while.
sentences.zh: 有一次，大约八年前，贝尔托内先生有一阵子没听到他的消息，便特意跑去他家。

sentences.en: George Bell cracked open the door, shooed him away.
sentences.zh: 乔治·贝尔把门打开一条缝，把他赶走了。

sentences.en: A curtain draped inside the entryway had camouflaged the chaos.
sentences.zh: 入口处挂着的一道帘子遮住了里面的混乱。

sentences.en: Mr. Bertone had no idea that at some point,
sentences.zh: 贝尔托内先生根本不知道，在某个时候，

sentences.en: George Bell had begun keeping everything.
sentences.zh: 乔治·贝尔开始把所有东西都留着。

sentences.en: The dude, Mr. Bertone, told the story.
sentences.zh: “老兄”贝尔托内先生讲述了这件事。

sentences.en: A few years ago, George Bell was going into the hospital for his heart and had asked him to hold on to some money,
sentences.zh: 几年前，乔治·贝尔因为心脏问题要住院，曾让他帮忙保管一些钱，

sentences.en: Gave him a fat envelope.
sentences.zh: 给了他一个厚厚的信封。

sentences.en: Inside was $55,000.
sentences.zh: 里面有5.5万美元。

sentences.en: Mike Caron, the bartender, interrupted.
sentences.zh: 酒保迈克·卡伦插话道。

sentences.en: Two things about George.
sentences.zh: “关于乔治有两件事。”

sentences.en: He gave me $100 every Christmas, and he never went out to eat.
sentences.zh: “他每年圣诞节都给我100美元，而且他从不出去吃饭。”

sentences.en: He had confessed he was too embarrassed because he would have required three entrees.
sentences.zh: 他曾坦言自己很尴尬，因为他一个人得点三份主菜。

sentences.en: George Bell had diabetes and complained about a shoulder pain.
sentences.zh: 乔治·贝尔患有糖尿病，还抱怨肩膀疼。

sentences.en: He took pills but skipped them during the day, saying they made him feel like an idiot.
sentences.zh: 他吃药，但白天经常漏服，说吃药让他觉得自己像个傻瓜。

sentences.en: Both the dude and Mr. Karens sensed he felt he had been bullied too hard by life.
sentences.zh: “老兄”和卡伦先生都感觉到，他觉得生活对他太苛刻了。

sentences.en: George was in a lot of pain, Mr. Karens said.
sentences.zh: “乔治当时很痛苦，”卡伦先生说。

sentences.en: I think he was just waiting to die.
sentences.zh: “我觉得他只是在等死。”

sentences.en: Had lived enough.
sentences.zh: “他已经活够了。”

sentences.en: It was as if sadness had killed George Bell.
sentences.zh: 仿佛是悲伤杀死了乔治·贝尔。

sentences.en: His days had become predictable, an endless loop.
sentences.zh: 他的日子变得一成不变，陷入了无尽的循环。

sentences.en: He stayed cloistered inside.
sentences.zh: 他把自己关在屋里。

sentences.en: Neighbors heard the regular parade of delivery men who brought him his takeout meals.
sentences.zh: 邻居们听到了那些送外卖的人频繁地来来往往。

sentences.en: The last time the dude saw George Bell was about a week before his body was found.
sentences.zh: “老兄”最后一次见到乔治·贝尔是在他被发现去世前大约一周。

sentences.en: Frozen shrimp was on sale at the shopping center.
sentences.zh: 购物中心的冷冻虾在打折。

sentences.en: George Bell got some to take back to the kitchen he did not use.
sentences.zh: 乔治·贝尔买了一些，带回了他根本不用的厨房。

sentences.en: Mr. Bertone didn't realize he had died until someone came to Legends with the news.
sentences.zh: 贝尔托内先生直到有人来到传奇酒吧带来消息，才知道他去世了。

sentences.en: Mr. Cairns was there, and he told the dude.
sentences.zh: 卡恩斯先生当时也在场，他告诉了“老兄”。

sentences.en: They made some calls to find out more, but got nowhere.
sentences.zh: 他们打了一些电话想了解更多情况，但一无所获。

sentences.en: Why did he die alone?
sentences.zh: 他为什么会孤独地死去？

sentences.en: No one knowing.
sentences.zh: 无人知晓。

sentences.en: The dude thought on that.
sentences.zh: “老兄”陷入了沉思。

sentences.en: I don't know, man, he said.
sentences.zh: “我不知道，伙计，”他说。

sentences.en: I wish I could tell you, but I don't know.
sentences.zh: “我希望能告诉你，但我真的不知道。”

sentences.en: On the televisions above the busy bar, a woman was promoting a cleaning product.
sentences.zh: 在繁忙的酒吧上方的电视机里，一位女士正在推销清洁产品。

sentences.en: In the dim light, Mr. Bertone emptied his drink.
sentences.zh: 在昏暗的灯光下，贝尔托内先生喝干了杯中的酒。

sentences.en: You know, I miss him, he said.
sentences.zh: “你知道吗，我很想念他，”他说。

sentences.en: I would have liked to see George one more time.
sentences.zh: “我真希望能再见乔治一面。”

sentences.en: It was my friend.
sentences.zh: “那可是我的朋友。”

sentences.en: One more time.
sentences.zh: “再见一面。”

sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会因为喝醉而睡着。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？
